record.title: Discrete–continuum exponent conjecture for separable permutations and cographs
record.statement:
Let $d(1/2)\in[\alpha_*(1/2),\beta^*(1/2)]$ be the exponent from the critical exponent conjecture. Let $\sigma_n$ be a uniform separable permutation of size $n$, and let $G_n$ be a uniform separable cograph of size $n$. Write $\operatorname{LIS}$ for longest increasing subsequence length and $\operatorname{LHS}$ for largest homogeneous-set size.

**Discrete–continuum exponent conjecture.** With probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$,

$$
\operatorname{LIS}(\sigma_n)=n^{d(1/2)+o(1)}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\operatorname{LHS}(G_n)=n^{d(1/2)+o(1)}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the exact polynomial exponent for the Brownian models at parameter $1/2$ also governs the corresponding uniform discrete models. Establishing this transfer is left open in the paper.
record.source_name: Jacopo Borga, William Da Silva and Ewain Gwynne, “Power-law bounds for increasing subsequences in Brownian separable permutons and homogeneous sets in Brownian cographons”, arXiv:2303.17030 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17030

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2023). “This conjecture is still open, see for a survey and for the best-known bound.”

record.title: Betke–Henk–Wills–Malikiosis discrete Minkowski conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K\in\mathcal K^n$ be a full-dimensional convex body and let $\Lambda\in\mathcal L^n$. Let $K_s$ be the symmetrization of $K$, and let $\operatorname{G}(K,\Lambda)=\#(K\cap\Lambda)$. **Discrete Minkowski conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{G}(K,\Lambda)\leq\prod_{i=1}^n\left\lfloor\frac{2}{\lambda_i(K_s,\Lambda)}+1\right\rfloor.
$$

The source presents this as a conjectural strengthening of the known bound involving only the first successive minimum and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Iskander Aliev and Martin Henk, “Minkowski's successive minima in convex and discrete geometry”, arXiv:2304.00120 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.00120

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “To generalize to the setting of arbitrary lattices is still an open problem.”

record.title: The tree-coloring strong spatial mixing conjecture
record.statement: Let $T$) be a tree of maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $q$ be the number of colors. The uniform distribution on proper $q$-colorings of $T$ is considered with strong spatial mixing (SSM), meaning that the influence of differing boundary pinnings on a vertex's marginal decays exponentially in their distance. **Tree-coloring SSM conjecture.** For $q \geq \Delta+1$, the uniform distribution on $q$-colorings on trees of maximum degree $\Delta$ exhibits strong spatial mixing with exponential decay rate. This is a basic unresolved question even on trees and is closely connected to understanding correlations in random colorings and to algorithmic sampling.
record.source_name: Zongchen Chen, Kuikui Liu, Nitya Mani and Ankur Moitra, “Strong spatial mixing for colorings on trees and its algorithmic applications”, arXiv:2304.01954 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.01954

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “It is surprising that such a basic question is still open, even on trees, but then again it also highlights how much we still have to learn about random colorings.”

record.title: Jerrum's Glauber-dynamics conjecture for graph colorings
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph of maximum degree $\Delta$, and consider the Glauber dynamics for sampling proper $q$-colorings of $G$. **Jerrum's conjecture.** The Glauber dynamics for sampling $q$-colorings from $G$ mixes in polynomial time whenever $q \geq \Delta+2$. Efficient Glauber-dynamics sampling at this threshold would substantially improve the best general bounds for approximate sampling of proper colorings; the paper reports that the conjecture remains open, with known results requiring more colors.

record.title: The normalized Laplacian maximum-connectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n\geq2$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{L}(G)$ be its normalized Laplacian matrix with eigenvalues

$$
0=\lambda_1(G)\leq\lambda_2(G)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n(G).
$$

**Normalized Laplacian maximum-connectivity conjecture.**

$$
\max\{\lambda_2(G),\lambda_2(G^c)\}\geq \frac{2}{n-1}.
$$

This is a normalized-Laplacian analogue of the Laplacian spread problem and concerns how well-connected a graph or its complement must be. Numerical computations motivate the bound, which remains open.
record.source_name: J. Nolan Faught, Mark Kempton and Adam Knudson, “A Nordhaus-Gaddum type problem for the normalized Laplacian spectrum and graph Cheeger constant”, arXiv:2304.01979 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.01979

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “The most obvious open problems are to prove Conjecture and Conjecture .”

record.title: The equality characterization for the normalized Laplacian maximum bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n\geq5$ vertices, with normalized Laplacian eigenvalues $0=\lambda_1(G)\leq\lambda_2(G)\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n(G)$. **Normalized Laplacian maximum-bound conjecture.**

$$
\max\{\lambda_2(G),\lambda_2(G^c)\}\geq\frac{2}{n-1}
$$

with equality if and only if $n$ is odd and $G$ is the join of an isolated vertex with two complete graphs, each of order $\frac{n-1}{2}$. This conjecture refines the proposed lower bound by specifying all equality cases. The paper presents it as an open problem supported by computations and identifies the displayed graph family for odd orders.

record.title: The connected-complement normalized Laplacian sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\lambda_2(G)$ denote the second-smallest eigenvalue of its normalized Laplacian. **Connected-complement normalized Laplacian conjecture.** If $G$ and $G^c$ are both connected, then

$$
\lambda_2(G)+\lambda_2(G^c)\geq\frac{2}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a stronger sum bound under the assumption that both a graph and its complement are connected. It is motivated by computational scatterplots and is explicitly identified as an open problem in the paper.

record.title: Harcos–Soltész conjecture on $K_{2,4}$-creating Hamilton paths
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $H_n(G)$ be the maximum number of Hamilton paths in $K_n$ such that the union of any two contains $G$ as a subgraph. In particular, $H_n(K_{2,4})$ is the corresponding maximum for the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,4}$.

**Harcos–Soltész conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
H_n(K_{2,4})\le C^n.
$$

The conjecture is equivalent to the reversing permutations conjecture. It would substantially improve the paper's upper bound, which is only of order $n^{n/2+o(n)}$ up to an exponential factor.

record.title: The characterization conjecture for 2-extremal digraphs
record.statement: Let $\mathcal H_2$ be the smallest class of digraphs containing symmetric odd cycles and closed under taking directed Hajós joins and $2$-Hajós tree joins. A digraph is **$2$-extremal** when it has the relevant extremal colouring property defined in the paper. **Characterization conjecture.** A digraph is $2$-extremal if and only if it belongs to $\mathcal H_2$. The paper observes that digraphs in $\mathcal H_2$ are $2$-extremal; the converse, which would characterize all $2$-extremal digraphs, remains conjectural.

record.title: Cap-counting conjecture for Galois affine planes
record.statement:
Let $I'_q$ be the maximum number of caps in a Galois affine plane $A(2,q)$. A **cap** is a set of points containing no three collinear points. **Cap-counting conjecture.** As $q\to\infty$,

$$
I'_q=2^{(1+o(1))q}.
$$

The conjecture aims to determine the number of caps in Desarguesian finite affine planes. The source gives the bounds $2^{q+1}<I'_q<2^{6q}$ and states that a substantial gap remains, so the conjecture is open.
record.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Jacques Verstraete, “Coloring hypergraphs that are the union of nearly disjoint cliques”, arXiv:2304.04855 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.04855

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2023). “Classical old open questions in projective geometry ask for the maximum size of caps in various projective spaces.”

record.title: Benevides, Łuczak, Scott, Skokan and White's long monochromatic cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)\geq\frac{3}{4}n$, and write

$$
n=3t+r,\qquad r\in\{0,1,2\}.
$$

A **2-edge-coloring** assigns one of two colors to every edge of $G$. **Benevides, Łuczak, Scott, Skokan and White's conjecture.** Every 2-edge-coloring of $G$ contains a monochromatic cycle of length at least $2t+r$. This conjecture was proposed after their result establishing the preceding cycle assertion apart from one special 2-edge-coloring, and remains open.
record.source_name: Yiran Zhang and Yuejian Peng, “Monochromatic cycles in 2-edge-colored bipartite graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:2304.08003 (2024).

record.title: Schelp's minimum-degree Ramsey conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices, and let $r(P_n,P_n)$ be its two-color Ramsey number. Set

$$
t=r(P_n,P_n),
$$

where $n$ is sufficiently large. A graph **arrows** $(P_n,P_n)$ when every 2-edge-coloring of it contains a monochromatic copy of $P_n$. **Schelp's conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph of order $t$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)>\frac{3}{4}t$, then

$$
G\longmapsto(P_n,P_n).
$$

The conjecture asks whether the minimum-degree condition forces the same monochromatic path Ramsey property at the order equal to the Ramsey number; its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Yiran Zhang and Yuejian Peng, “Monochromatic cycles in 2-edge-colored bipartite graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:2304.08003 (2024).

record.title: Maximum-criterion conjecture for linear-fragmentation processes
record.statement:
A linear-fragmentation process is a continuous process with finite mean, variance, and third moment. **Maximum-criterion conjecture.** Every linear-fragmentation process satisfies the maximum criterion in all dimensions

$$
1 \leq d \leq m.
$$

The maximum criterion is the assumption used in the paper's theorem on the Benfordness of the maximum measurement. This conjecture proposes that the criterion holds broadly for continuous linear-fragmentation processes with the stated moment conditions; the source does not report a resolution.

record.title: Uniqueness of the optimal arithmetic distribution for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth problem
record.statement:
An **arithmetic probability distribution** is a probability distribution arising as an arithmetic limiting measure, and let $\lambda^{SSS}$ denote the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace infimum. The notation $\mathbb R^+$ denotes the nonnegative real numbers.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** There is a unique arithmetic probability distribution $\mu_{SSS}$ compactly supported in $\mathbb R^+$ such that

$$
\int x\,d\mu_{SSS}=\lambda^{SSS}.
$$

This asks whether the optimal distribution for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem is unique; it is presented as an open question, and the paper notes that the method gives finite analogues but does not determine an explicit value of $\lambda^{SSS}$.

record.title: Maximum-degree conjecture for critically frustrated signed graphs
record.statement:
Let $(G,\sigma)$ be a critically $k$-frustrated signed graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$. A cycle is **negative** when the product of the signs on its edges is negative.

**Maximum-degree conjecture.** Every critically $k$-frustrated signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ satisfies

$$
\Delta(G)\leq 2k.
$$

Moreover, equality $\Delta(G)=2k$ can occur only when $G$ consists of $k$ negative cycles that are pairwise edge-disjoint but all contain the same vertex.

This conjecture proposes both a universal maximum-degree bound and a characterization of the equality case; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Chiara Cappello, Reza Naserasr, Eckhard Steffen and Zhouningxin Wang, “Critically 3-frustrated signed graphs”, arXiv:2304.10243 (2023).

record.title: e-positivity conjecture for the symmetric functions g_k of Hessenberg graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{m}\colon[n]\to[n]$ be a Hessenberg function, let $G_\mathbf{m}$ be its indifference graph, and let $g_k(G_\mathbf{m};x,q)$ be the symmetric functions defined in the paper. A symmetric function is **e-positive** if it is a nonnegative linear combination of elementary symmetric functions. **e-positivity conjecture for the functions $g_k$.** The symmetric functions $g_k(G_\mathbf{m};x,q)$ are e-positive for every Hessenberg function $\mathbf{m}\colon[n]\to[n]$ and every $k=0,\ldots,n-1$.

This conjecture is motivated by the identity expressing the chromatic quasisymmetric function in terms of the functions $g_k$: e-positivity of all the $g_k$ would imply e-positivity of the chromatic quasisymmetric function and therefore the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Alex Abreu and Antonio Nigro, “Splitting the cohomology of Hessenberg varieties and e-positivity of chromatic symmetric functions”, arXiv:2304.10644 (2023).
record.references:

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2023). “This conjecture has since been proven by Brosnan--Chow () and Guay-Pacquet ().”

record.title: An upper-bound conjecture for the essential spectral radius index
record.statement:
Let $C_N^m$ be a regular ring lattice satisfying the assumptions of the spectral-radius theorem, and let $j^{\star}$ denote the index used to compute the essential spectral radius. For $N\geq 4$ and $m\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, define

$$
\overline{j}=\left\lceil \frac{3N}{4m+2}-\frac12\right\rceil.
$$

**Upper-bound conjecture for $j^{\star}$.** There exists $\overline{j}\in\{2,\ldots,n\}$ such that

$$
j^{\star}\leq\overline{j},
$$

and its expression is

$$
\overline{j}=\left\lceil \frac{3N}{4m+2}-\frac12\right\rceil,\qquad \forall N\geq4,\ \forall m\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}.
$$

This conjectured bound would provide an analytic upper bound for the index determining the essential spectral radius of the Randić matrix of a regular ring lattice, complementing the previously established lower bound.
record.source_name: Marco Fabris, “On the Characterization of Regular Ring Lattices and their Relation with the Dirichlet Kernel”, arXiv:2304.11602 (2023).

record.title: The weak Malle conjecture over the rationals
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a transitive subgroup of $S_n$. Let $\mathcal F_n(X;G)$ be the set of degree-$n$ number fields $K$ satisfying

$$
[K:\mathbb Q]=n,\qquad \operatorname{Gal}(\hat K/\mathbb Q)=G,\qquad |\Delta_K|\leqslant X,
$$

where $\hat K$ is the Galois closure of $K$ over $\mathbb Q$, and equality of Galois groups is up to conjugacy as permutation groups on the $n$ embeddings of $K$. Write $F_n(X;G)=|\mathcal F_n(X;G)|$. Define

$$
\operatorname{ind}(G)=\min\{\operatorname{ind}(g):1\ne g\in G\},
$$

where $n-\operatorname{ind}(g)$ is the number of orbits of $g$ on $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and set $a(G)=\operatorname{ind}(G)^{-1}$. **Weak Malle conjecture over the rationals.** For every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
X^{a(G)}\ll_n F_n(X;G)\ll_{n,\varepsilon}X^{a(G)+\varepsilon}.
$$

This is a weakened form of Malle's conjecture, stated in response to Klüners's counterexample to the original formulation. The source attributes this version to Alb20; the general conjecture is not presented as resolved here.
record.source_name: Sam Chow and Rainer Dietmann, “Enumerative Galois theory for number fields”, arXiv:2304.11991 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11991

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

record.title: Maximum-period conjecture for the logistic map over $\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}$
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}$ be the ring of residue classes modulo $3^n$, and consider the logistic map

$$
f_{3^n}(x)=\mu x(x+1)\bmod 3^n,
$$

where $\mu,x\in\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}$. For an initial value $x_0\in\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}$, let $L(x_0;\mu,3^n)$ denote the period of the resulting sequence, and define

$$
L(\mu,3^n)=\max\{L(x_0;\mu,3^n)\mid x_0\in\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}\}.
$$

**Maximum-period conjecture.** When $\mu\bmod 3=1$, the maximum period is

$$
L(\mu,3^n)=3^{n-2}.
$$

The claim concerns the corrected formula for the maximum period of the logistic map over $\mathbb{Z}_{3^n}$; the source states that an earlier representation does not hold in several residue cases and says that this conjecture is proved later in the paper as a corollary.
record.source_name: Xiaoxiong Lu, Eric Yong Xie and Chengqing Li, “Periodicity Analysis of the Logistic Map over Ring Z_3^n”, arXiv:2304.12193 (2023).

record.title: Larrión–Neumann-Lara–Pizaña conjecture on clique divergence of non-negative Euler characteristic surfaces
record.statement: Let $G$ be a locally cyclic graph of minimum degree $\delta\ge 4$ triangulating a closed surface of Euler characteristic $\chi\ge 0$; equivalently, the surface is a sphere, projective plane, torus or Klein bottle. A graph is **clique divergent** if its clique dynamics does not eventually cycle. **Larrión–Neumann-Lara–Pizaña's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is clique divergent. This conjecture asks whether every such triangulation has divergent clique dynamics; the paper presents it as an open question and attributes it to Larrión, Neumann-Lara and Pizaña.
record.source_name: Anna M. Limbach and Martin Winter, “Characterising Clique Convergence for Locally Cyclic Graphs of Minimum Degree δ6”, arXiv:2305.00503 (2025).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2023). “Various other open questions emerge from the context of graph coverings.”

record.title: Clique convergence conjecture for locally cyclic triangulations of a disc
record.statement: Let $G$ be a locally cyclic graph with boundary and minimum degree $\delta\ge 4$ triangulating a disc. Such a graph is **clique null** if its clique dynamics converges to the one-vertex graph. **Disc convergence conjecture.** The graph $G$ is clique convergent; in fact, it is clique null. This conjecture concerns the exceptional compact surface with boundary that is not covered by the known existence of clique-divergent triangulations, and the paper presents it as an open conjecture.

record.title: Exact formula for the minimal length of a geodesic with at least k self-intersections
record.statement:
Let $M_k$ be the infimum of lengths of geodesics with self-intersection number at least $k$ among all finite-type hyperbolic surfaces. A **minimal-length geodesic conjecture** asserts that, for $k\geqslant 1$,

$$
M_k=2\cosh^{-1}(1+2k)=2\log(1+2k+2\sqrt{k^2+k}).
$$

Moreover, equality is attained when $\Gamma$ is a corkscrew geodesic on a thrice-punctured sphere. This refines Basmajian's logarithmic bounds for $M_k$ by proposing an exact value and an explicit extremal surface and geodesic; the supplied text does not indicate whether the claim has been proved or remains open.

record.title: Hitting time conjecture for connectivity in the W-edge-incremental process
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a connected graphon and $K\in\mathbb{N}$. For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, consider the $W$-edge-incremental process $\mathfrak{X}_n=(G_n^t)_{t=0}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ of order $n$. Let $f_n$ and $g_n$ be the hitting times in this process for the properties of being $K$-connected and having minimum degree $K$, respectively. **Hitting time conjecture.** Asymptotically almost surely, 

$$
f_n=g_n.
$$

This extends the Erdős–Rényi hitting-time result to the inhomogeneous setting and to higher minimum degree and connectivity. The conjecture concerns the edge-incremental process associated with a connected graphon.
record.source_name: Jan Hladký and Gopal Viswanathan, “Connectivity of inhomogeneous random graphs II”, arXiv:2305.03607 (2026).

record.title: Graded-ring conjecture for absorbing ideals
record.statement:
Let $R=\bigoplus_{g\in G}R_g$ be a ring graded by a torsion-free abelian group $G$. Let $\alpha$ be an ideal of $R$, and let $\alpha^*$ be the largest homogeneous ideal contained in $\alpha$. For an ideal $\beta$, let $\omega(\beta)$ denote its absorbing number.

**Graded-ring conjecture.** For any ideal $\alpha$ of a graded ring $R$,

$$
\omega(\alpha^*)\leq\omega(\alpha).
$$

This is motivated by the fact that the homogeneous part of a prime ideal is prime, and asks whether the analogous inequality holds for absorbing ideals. The source does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Spencer Secord, “Collections of an Ideal: Any n-Absorbing Ideal is Strongly n-Absorbing”, arXiv:2305.03878 (2023).

record.title: Zero-distribution conjecture for generated Taylor polynomials with nonpositive discriminant
record.statement:
Let $\{P_m(z)\}_{m\geq 0}$ be a sequence of functions of $z$ generated by

$$
\sum_{m=0}^\infty P_m(z)t^m=\frac{1}{(at^2+bt+c)(1-tz)}.
$$

Here $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$ and $b^2-4ac\leq 0$. Let $t_1$ be the zero of $at^2+bt+c$ having smallest modulus, and let $\mathcal{Z}(P_m)$ denote the zero set of $P_m$. **Zero-distribution conjecture.**

$$
\lim \mathcal{Z}(P_m)=\left\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=\frac{1}{|t_1|}\right\}.
$$

The claim concerns the limiting distribution of zeros for the generating-function sequence in the case where the quadratic has nonpositive discriminant. The paper's conclusions indicate that the complex-zero case remains to be handled, and the parser supplied no resolution evidence, so the status is left open.
record.source_name: Juhoon Chung, “Zero Distribution of Generated Taylor Polynomials”, arXiv:2305.05130 (2023).

record.title: Logarithmic path-length conjecture for the (1,1) edge-removal process
record.statement:
Consider the task-dependency graph generated on $n$ vertices by the $(1,1)$ edge-removal process, and let its maximum directed path length be measured in expectation.

**Logarithmic path-length conjecture.** The expected maximum directed path length of the resulting task-dependency graph is

$$
\Theta(\log n).
$$

The conjecture is based on experimental results suggesting logarithmic growth in $n$, in contrast to the apparently linear growth for the edge-addition process. No resolution is provided in the source.

record.title: Connected transversal threshold conjecture for complete multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 4$, let $K_r$ be the complete graph on $r$ parts, and let $\mathcal{T}_r$ denote the family of all trees on $r$ vertices. For an $r$-partite graph, write $\pi_{K_r}(\mathcal{T}_r)$ for the smallest $r$-partite density forcing a connected transversal tree.

**Connected transversal conjecture.** The lower bound in Theorem~ is tight. In particular, for any $r\geq 4$, every $r$-partite graph with $r$-partite density at least $\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ contains a transversal tree on $r$ vertices.

The conjecture would determine the connected-transversal density threshold for complete multipartite graphs, improving the presently established bounds.

record.title: The VOSA-to-$\mathrm{TMF}$ class conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{V}$ be a holomorphic VOSA of central charge $n/2$ containing an affine algebra $\hat{\mathfrak{g}}_k$. Let $G$ be the simply-connected compact Lie group of type $\mathfrak{g}$, and let $\tau\colon BG\to K(\mathbb{Z},4)$ represent a generator of $H^4(BG;\mathbb{Z})\simeq\mathbb{Z}$. Then

**The VOSA-to-$\operatorname{TMF}$ class conjecture.** The VOSA should determine a class

$$
[\mathbb{V}]\in \operatorname{TMF}^{n+k\tau}_G(\mathrm{pt}),
$$

such that $\Phi([\mathbb{V}])\in \operatorname{KO}^n_G((q))(\mathrm{pt})$ can be computed from the theory of VOSAs. This proposes a mathematical realization of the Stolz–Teichner correspondence for purely left-moving theories, but genuinely equivariant twisted $\operatorname{TMF}$ was not yet adequately developed in the source.

record.title: Maximum hyperplane intersection conjecture for odd-dimensional permutohedra
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the permutohedron, and let $H_0$ be its affine hull. For an affine hyperplane $H\ne H_0$, consider the number of vertices in $H\cap P_n$. **Maximum intersection conjecture.** If $n$ is odd, then every hyperplane different from $H_0$ contains at most $(n-1)!$ points of $P_n$. This bound would explain the lower bound in the preceding covering conjecture for odd $n$; the source presents the assertion as an unproved belief.

record.title: Linear-order conjecture for immersions of transitive tournaments in tournaments
record.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer. A **tournament** is an orientation of a complete graph, and an **immersion** of a transitive tournament on $k$ vertices consists of $k$ branch vertices together with pairwise edge-disjoint directed paths representing all edges of the transitive tournament. **Linear-order immersion conjecture.** Every tournament on at least $(2+o(1))k$ vertices contains an immersion of a transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. The question asks for the precise order of the largest tournament avoiding such an immersion. The authors indicate that their methods do not determine the optimal constant, so the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Vasconcelos' SCM conjecture for height-three homogeneous ideals
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a polynomial ring and let $I$ be a homogeneous ideal of height $3$. Write $\mu(I)$ for the minimum number of generators, let $g=\operatorname{ht}(I)$, and define the deviation of $I$ to be $\mu(I)-g$. Say that $I$ is generically a complete intersection, that $I$ is Gorenstein, and that the resolution of $S/I$ is pure. Finally, $I$ is strongly Cohen--Macaulay (SCM) when all its Koszul homology modules are Cohen--Macaulay.

**Vasconcelos' SCM conjecture.** If $I$ has deviation at least $3$, is generically a complete intersection, is not Gorenstein, and the resolution of $S/I$ is pure, then $I$ is not SCM.

The text says that numerical computations and cited results support this conjecture and explicitly states that it is still open.
record.source_name: Maria Vaz Pinto and Rafael H. Villarreal, “Graph rings and ideals: Wolmer Vasconcelos' contributions”, arXiv:2305.06270 (2025).

record.title: Strong orientation conjecture for maximum total arc-connectivity
record.statement: Let $G$ be a 2-edge-connected graph, let $\vec{G}$ be an orientation of $G$, and let $tac(\vec{G})$ denote its total arc-connectivity. An orientation **maximizes total arc-connectivity** when it maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ among all orientations of $G$. An orientation is **strong** when the resulting digraph is strongly connected. **Strong orientation conjecture.** Every 2-edge-connected graph $G$ has an orientation $\vec{G}$ that maximizes $tac(\vec{G})$ and is strong. The conjecture asks whether maximum total arc-connectivity can always be attained by a strongly connected orientation; the source calls it plausible and gives no resolution.

record.title: The equivalence of nuclearity, symmetric amenability, strong amenability and unitary-group amenability
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital, separable $C^*$-algebra. The **QTS property** means that every non-trivial quotient of $A$ admits a non-trivial trace. The unitary group of $A$ is denoted by ${\rm U}(A)$, and ${\rm U}_0(A)$ denotes its connected component of the identity. A topological group is amenable if its bounded right-uniformly continuous functions admit a left invariant mean, and skew-amenable if they admit a right invariant mean.

**Amenability equivalence conjecture.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $A$ is nuclear and has the QTS property.
2. $A$ is symmetrically amenable.
3. $A$ is strongly amenable.
4. ${\rm U}(A)$ is amenable in the norm topology.
5. ${\rm U}(A)$ is skew-amenable in the weak topology.

Nuclearity is already known to characterize weak-topology amenability of the unitary group, while symmetric amenability is known to be equivalent to nuclearity together with the QTS property. The conjecture proposes that these properties also coincide with strong amenability and the stated norm- and weak-topology amenability properties of the unitary group.
record.source_name: Vadim Alekseev, Max Schmidt and Andreas Thom, “Amenability for unitary groups of C*-algebras”, arXiv:2305.13181 (2024).

record.title: Improved dimension dependence for approximate matchings
record.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be persistence modules that are $\epsilon$-interleaved, with $\epsilon\geq 0$. Let

$$
r=\sup_{M'\in B(M)}\operatorname{supdim}M'<\infty.
$$

Here $B(M)$ is the relevant neighborhood of $M$ defined in the paper, and an $\epsilon$-refinement is the paper's approximate decomposition relation. **The improved-dimension conjecture.** There is a constant $c\geq 0$, independent of $M$, $N$, $\epsilon$, and $r$, and a module $Q$ that is both a $cr\epsilon$-refinement of $M$ and a $cr\epsilon$-refinement of $N$.

This conjecture seeks to improve the main theorem's dependence on the maximum pointwise dimension of $M$ by using the dimensions of modules in $B(M)$. It is presented as open and is the main conjectural strengthening motivating later special cases.

record.title: Bounded tree-independence conjecture for (even hole, diamond)-free graphs
record.statement: An **(even hole, diamond)-free graph** is a graph containing neither an even hole nor a diamond as an induced subgraph. Its tree independence number is denoted by $\operatorname{tree-\alpha}(G)$. **Bounded tree-independence conjecture.** The class of (even hole, diamond)-free graphs has bounded tree independence number. record.title: Montiel–Urbano conjecture for the Clifford torus in the complex projective plane
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{C}P^2$ be the complex projective plane, let $\mathcal{W}$ be the Willmore functional, and let $\mathcal{W}^-$ denote its component arising from the twistor decomposition. The **Clifford torus** is

$$
T=\Big\{[z_1,z_2,z_3]\in\mathbb{C}P^2\,\Big|\,|z_1|=|z_2|=|z_3|\Big\}.
$$

**Montiel–Urbano conjecture.** The Clifford torus achieves the minimum of the functional $\mathcal{W}^-$, and hence of $\mathcal{W}$, either among all tori in $\mathbb{C}P^2$ or among all Lagrangian tori in $\mathbb{C}P^2$.

The conjecture concerns the global minimization of the conformally invariant Willmore functional in the complex projective plane. The paper establishes strict Willmore stability of the Clifford torus, providing evidence, but does not resolve the global minimization claim.
record.source_name: Changping Wang and Zhenxiao Xie, “Willmore surfaces in 4-dimensional conformal manifolds”, arXiv:2306.00846 (2025).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the smallest element of a $D(4)$-quadruple
record.statement:
Let $D(4)$-$m$-tuples be sets of distinct positive integers such that the product of any two distinct elements increased by $4$ is a perfect square. Suppose that $\{a_1,b,c,d\}$ is a $D(4)$-quadruple with

$$
a_1<b<c<d.
$$

**Smallest-element uniqueness conjecture.** Then $\{a_2,b,c,d\}$ is not a $D(4)$-quadruple for any integer $a_2$ with $a_1\neq a_2<b$.

This asserts that, after the three larger elements are fixed, a $D(4)$-quadruple cannot have a different smaller positive integer in place of its smallest element. The source presents the statement as a conjecture in the context of extensions of $D(4)$-triples by smaller elements; its resolution is not specified here.

record.title: Tail Conjecture for highest weights of $gl(m|n)$ modules
record.statement:
Let $\lambda\in \Lambda^+_{m|n}$. Let $\Sigma_\lambda\in\mathbb{S}$ be the base for which $\Phi(\lambda)=D_\lambda^{\Sigma_\lambda}$, define $\lambda^{\dagger}:=\lambda_{\Sigma_\lambda}$ and $\overline{\lambda}^{\dagger}:=\lambda^{\dagger}+\rho_{\Sigma_\lambda}$, and set

$$
tail(\lambda):=s\left(\overline{\lambda}^{\dagger}\right).
$$

For the module with highest weight $\lambda$, write

$$
longtail(\lambda):=\max_{\nu\in Hwt(\lambda)}s(\nu).
$$

**Tail Conjecture.** For any $\lambda\in\Lambda^+_{m|n}$,

$$
tail(\lambda)=longtail(\lambda).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the tail determined by the distinguished weight diagram equals the maximum tail over the highest weights associated with the module. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source material.

record.title: The circumference conjecture for connected matroid pathwidth
record.statement: Let $M$ be a connected matroid with rank function $r$. Its **circumference** is the maximum size of a circuit of $M$, when $M$ has at least one circuit, and its pathwidth is denoted by $\operatorname{pw}(M)$. **Connected matroid circumference conjecture.** Every connected matroid $M$ with circumference $k$ has pathwidth $O(k)$. This conjecture seeks a linear upper bound on the pathwidth of connected matroids in terms of their circumference, generalizing analogous bounds for $2$-connected graphs. The source does not state whether the conjecture is known or resolved.
